findings.title: READ issued to a bank one cycle after that bank was PRECHARGEd (no ACTIVATE between)
findings.requirement: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.expected: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.actual: PRE b=1 at cycle 183, RD b=1 at cycle 184.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 183 PRE bank 1 (A10=0), cycle 184 RD bank 1 col 0. The generated PROTO_001 tracker (row-open state from the observed ACT/PRE stream) shows bank 1 closed when the READ is issued. Never observed in simulation (no path stimulus reaches this interleaving); the scheduler or its bank_tracker gating lets a CAS follow its own precharge. Likely the same root as the open scheduler re-grant defect (commands are also held for 2-3 consecutive cycles in the trace, i.e. re-issued). [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on 3596e1ec698e]

findings.title: scheduler: PROTO_002
findings.requirement: ACTIVATE issued to a bank that already has an active row without intervening PRECHARGE. State convention: a bank is 'active' from its ACTIVATE until a PRECHARGE to it, or any REFRESH (which closes every bank whether or not it was legal, so an illegal REFRESH is reported once as REF_002 and does not cascade into this rule on the next ACTIVATE).

findings.title: scheduler: The scheduler selects from bank_tracker's permissions, but a command it issues only reaches bank_tracker three
findings.requirement: The scheduler selects from bank_tracker's permissions, but a command it issues only reaches bank_tracker three cycles later (scheduler output register -> cmd_gen register -> feedback). In that window the permissions are stale: the same bank is ACTIVATEd again (PROTO_002, tRC), another bank is ACTIVATEd inside tRRD, traffic resumes inside tRFC after a REFRESH, a bank is read right after it was precharged. The re-grant mask added in drop 5661e03 covers only the CAS dequeue.

findings.title: PRECHARGE issued one cycle after a WRITE to the same bank (tWR violated; write data lost)
findings.requirement: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.expected: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.actual: WR b=4 at cycle 173, PRE b=4 at cycle 174.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 173 WR bank 4, cycle 174 PRE bank 4. tWR = 15 ns = 3 controller cycles, so 2 cycles must separate the last write beat from the precharge. Not observed in simulation. bank_tracker's write-recovery timer (cfg_tWR_nCK) does not gate bank_pre_allowed for the cycle after a write, or the scheduler ignores it on the row-conflict path. [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on 3596e1ec698e]

findings.requirement: The manifest says bank_tracker.cmd_pre_bank is driven directly by cmd_gen.fb_pre_bank. It is not: cmd_gen's feedback interface carries a bank number only for ACTIVATE (fb_act_bank); its PRE/RD/WR pulses are bankless, yet bank_tracker needs cmd_pre_bank/cmd_rd_bank/cmd_wr_bank to track per-bank state

findings.mechanism: The manifest says bank_tracker.cmd_pre_bank is driven directly by cmd_gen.fb_pre_bank. It is not: cmd_gen's feedback interface carries a bank number only for ACTIVATE (fb_act_bank); its PRE/RD/WR pulses are bankless, yet bank_tracker needs cmd_pre_bank/cmd_rd_bank/cmd_wr_bank to track per-bank state. The harness registers the scheduler's cmd_bank one cycle so it aligns with the REGISTERED fb pulses. This is testbench glue standing in for a missing design signal — see the filed finding; the Frontend should add fb_pre_bank/fb_rd_bank/fb_wr_bank. Driver used: scheduler.cmd_bank. Either the RTL should consume cmd_gen.fb_pre_bank as declared, or the manifest should stop claiming a direct connection.

findings.requirement: A READ/WRITE must execute against the row its request asked for: when the CAS for a request issues, the row open in that bank (set by the most recent ACTIVATE to it) must be the request's row. An ACTIVATE that no pending request asked for is NOT a violation by itself — a controller may open a row speculatively — only a CAS landing on the wrong row is.

findings.title: scheduler: REF_002
findings.requirement: REFRESH issued while one or more banks are still active (not precharged). State convention: after any REFRESH every bank is treated as precharged (idle), legal or not -- a REFRESH issued with a bank open is this violation and RESYNCHRONISES the bank model; the ACTIVATE that follows is not a second violation.
